messages:
alex: Quick follow-up on the streaming coalesce scheduler RFC — I want to compare admission-gate (token-bucket) vs deadline-driven queuing tradeoffs. Are we comfortable with a hybrid?
maria: Leaning hybrid. Main concern is long-seq requests starving short ones when they join the coalesce window. Head-of-line blocking is real.
devin: Agreed. My sketch: per-tenant soft token buckets + per-request deadline hint header. Use the hint to bump priority within the coalesce window.
sasha: How do we handle preemption? Can we demote a request mid-batch if deadline misses look likely? Preempting a GPU batch is expensive. :thinking:
devin: Preemption is rough on GPUs + KV cache. Instead of mid-batch preemption, we can do early-release: keep a micro-queue that flushes lower-priority items earlier if deadline quantile is tight. No kernel-level kill.
maria: That sounds fine. Also want a fast-path shallow queue for <32-token requests to avoid batching overhead. Surface that in routing.
alex: So two logical queues: fast-path (shallow, low-latency) and streaming-coalesce (deep, deadline-aware). Admission gate rules differ.
sasha: For fairness across tenants, we should track effective tokens and recent SLA violations, not just raw RPS. Otherwise noisy tenants steal bursts.
devin: Right — maintain a leaky counter of SLO breaches per tenant and reduce burst allowance when breaches exceed threshold. Basically soft backpressure.
maria: Pseudoconfig idea: 
```
admission_policy:
  mode: hybrid
  fast_path_threshold_tokens: 32
  token_bucket:
    rate_per_tenant: 100
    burst: 200
  deadline_quantile_max_ms: 120
  slo_penalty_window: 600
```
Keep it pluggable so we can tune without code churn.
alex: Need to simulate for mixed workloads (short chat, long-context summarization, embeddings). Sasha can you run a sim with 80% short, 20% long and measure p50/p95/p99 across tenants?
sasha: On it. I'll add a synthetic driver that models KV warm/cold cost and batch fill latency. Expect results in ~48h.
devin: One more: when model variants exist (quantized vs full), route over-capacity overflow to cheaper variant rather than delaying. Cheap fallback reduces tail latency.
maria: +1 for fallback routing, but must count it in quality/regression checks. Add metric tag for "fallback_used".
alex: Action items: prototype token-bucket + deadline header in scheduler (devin), simulation + numbers (sasha), RFC update with config examples and fallback rules (maria). I'll collect results and we can decide on rollout policy.
deploy-bot: RFC doc updated: https://redwood.internal/docs/rfc/streaming-coalesce-scheduler (edited) :white_check_mark:
alex: thanks everyone :thumbsup:
